content.user_title: Review Stripe Webhook Security and Retry Safety
content.value_statement: Stripe webhook mistakes can allow forged events, duplicate side effects, or lost payment updates. This skill guides read-only Next.js reviews with severity labels and concrete fixes.
actual_capabilities: Locate Next.js webhook handlers and inspect the helpers they call.
Check Stripe signature verification and raw-body handling before events are trusted.
Review event.id tracking, pending/completed states, and retries after failed processing.
Check overlapping deliveries for idempotent writes, atomic leases, and side-effect deduplication.
Review subscription item selection, checkout identity validation, and runtime suitability.
Produce a severity summary, file-and-line findings table, suggested fixes, and verification gaps.
limitations: The checks are heuristics, not proof of vulnerabilities or a complete security audit.
The skill does not run webhook deliveries, database concurrency tests, or Stripe API validation.
Unavailable helpers, queue workers, and external packages can prevent complete verification.
Reviews are read-only; fixes require a separate user request.

use_cases.title: Review payment handlers before launch
use_cases.description: Check signature verification, raw-body handling, and event tracking before deploying a Next.js payment integration.

use_cases.title: Investigate duplicate processing
use_cases.description: Review pending events, leases, and side-effect deduplication when retries appear to repeat emails or credit grants.

use_cases.title: Assess subscription entitlement changes
use_cases.description: Review subscription item selection and checkout identity validation during billing changes or a multi-item subscription migration.

prompt_templates.title: Basic webhook review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Next.js Stripe webhook handlers without editing files. List findings by severity, include file references, and explain anything you cannot verify.

prompt_templates.title: Verify event authenticity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review signature verification and raw-body handling in my Stripe webhook routes. Check that unverified events cannot reach processing and verification failures return 400.

prompt_templates.title: Audit retry behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace event.id tracking through handlers and helpers. Review pending/completed transitions, failed attempts, concurrent deliveries, leases, and side-effect deduplication. Do not edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Review the complete billing workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review webhook handlers, claim/complete helpers, and available queue workers. Check item-specific entitlements and checkout identity validation. Distinguish verified findings from unavailable evidence.

output_examples.input: Review a handler that trusts parsed event data without signature verification.
output: Critical, S1: The handler trusts events without Stripe signature verification.
Critical, S2: Parsing JSON before verification does not preserve the raw signed body.
Suggested fix: Verify the raw body, signature, and endpoint secret before processing. Return 400 when verification fails.

output_examples.input: Review a handler that returns 200 for every previously recorded event, including failed pending attempts.
output: Medium, S6: Status-blind deduplication prevents failed pending events from retrying.
Suggested fix: Track pending and completed states. Protect reprocessing with idempotent writes or an atomic lease and deduplicate side effects.
Verification gap: Queue worker behavior cannot be assessed when its implementation is unavailable.

best_practices: Provide webhook handlers and their claim, completion, synchronization, and queue helpers for a connected review.
Include the Stripe API version and entitlement mapping when reviewing multi-item subscriptions.
Treat findings as review prompts and verify proposed changes with signature, retry, and concurrent-delivery tests.
anti_patterns: Treating a heuristic finding as proof without inspecting the referenced handler and helpers.
Reprocessing pending events with non-idempotent side effects and no lease or deduplication key.
Assuming the first subscription item always controls entitlements in a multi-item subscription.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js Stripe webhook handlers in App Router routes and Pages Router API handlers, including their processing helpers.

faq.question: Does the skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It performs a read-only review unless you subsequently request fixes.

faq.question: Does it test live Stripe deliveries?
faq.answer: No. It reviews available source code and reports checks that it cannot verify.

faq.question: What does the review report include?
faq.answer: It includes handlers reviewed, severity counts, check identifiers, file-and-line references, suggested fixes, and verification gaps.

faq.question: Are all pending-event retries unsafe?
faq.answer: No. The skill checks for non-idempotent work without a lease or deduplication key before flagging pending-event reprocessing.

faq.question: Can it guarantee payment security?
faq.answer: No. Its checks are heuristics and do not replace broader security review, integration tests, or concurrency testing.
